content: HELB’s USSD Self Serve Option lets Kenyan students access certain HELB services using an MPESA number registered under their name and ID. To use it for withdrawing funds, dial *642#, register and choose a PIN you can remember, then dial *642# again to log in and select “withdraw funds.” Choose the upkeep option and enter the amount you want to withdraw, then enter your MPESA PIN to complete the transaction. You will receive an MPESA confirmation message. A Ksh. 15 charge applies per transaction. For applying for a subsequent loan, dial *642#, log in with your PIN, select the loan application option, choose your application level (Degree or Diploma Certificate), select the academic year, and send. If you need more FAQs or other services, verify details on HELB’s official USSD page. [1]

HELB Products: Financing Your Education

Education can be expensive, but the Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides a smarter way to finance your studies. Whether you are heading to a university or a TVET institution, HELB is designed to support your academic journey.

HELB Loans

If you are looking to further your education, applying for a HELB loan allows you to afford your studies while benefiting from low interest rates. The available loan products include:

TVET Loans: Specifically designed for students enrolled in Technical and Vocational Education and Training institutions.

Undergraduate Loans: Tailored for students pursuing degree programs at recognized universities.

Jielimishe Loans: An additional financing option provided by HELB to assist students in meeting their educational costs.

HELB Scholarships

For students seeking financial aid beyond loans, HELB provides information on various scholarship options and sources available for those studying in Kenya. These include:

ABSA Scholarships: Opportunities for eligible students.

Visa Oshwal Aid: Financial support programs for qualifying students.

Post Graduate Scholarship: Dedicated support for students pursuing advanced degrees.

Partner Funds

HELB has established partnerships with several local and international organizations to assist promising but needy students across Kenya. These funds are critical for students who require extra support to continue their studies after secondary school. Current partner funds include:

HELB Afya Elimu Fund
Civil Servants Training Revolving Fund (TRF)
AIC Kijabe Hospital Fund
Tenwek Hospital Fund
Simba Foundation Fund
ST. Kiz

How to Access HELB Services

HELB provides a centralized digital experience for all users. Students, loanees, institutions, employers, and debt collectors can access specific portals directly through the official HELB website. Key self-service features available on the platform include:

Self Serve: Manage your account and personal details.
Compliance Certificate: Access and download your compliance documentation.
Get-In-Touch: Reach out to HELB for support or inquiries.

What Students Should Do Now

If you are planning to apply for funding, visit the official HELB website at https://www.helb.co.ke/products/ to review the specific requirements and application procedures for each product. Because eligibility criteria and application deadlines can vary by program, you should verify all details directly on the official portal rather than relying on third-party information. Ensure your documentation is ready and monitor the student portal regularly for updates regarding your application status.

Always use the official HEF portal to track application windows and submit requests, and never pay individuals to process your application [4][1][5].

content:
UNDERGRADUATE LOANS: HELB GUIDELINES

The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides financial support to students pursuing Bachelor’s degrees. This support is intended for students enrolled in Public and Chartered Private Universities within the East African Community. Eligibility covers students placed through the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS) as well as self-sponsored, parallel, and Module II students. Please note that pre-university, certificate, diploma, and postgraduate students are not eligible to apply for this specific loan.

KEY LOAN DETAILS

These loans are interest-bearing, currently set at a rate of 4% per annum, and include an annual ledger fee of Kshs. 1,000. The duration of loan eligibility is tied directly to the length of your academic program. For example, a student enrolled in a four-year degree program is eligible for four years of funding, while a five-year program qualifies for five years of support. 

APPLICATION TYPES

There are two primary categories for loan applications: 
First-time applicants are those applying for the initial year of their degree program. 
Second and subsequent applicants are those returning to the board for their second, third, or fourth year of study, depending on the remaining duration of their course.

HOW TO APPLY

Students are advised to initiate their application at least one month before the academic term begins to ensure sufficient processing time. To apply, you must visit the official HELB student portal at hef.co.ke. Once on the site, click on the register option to create your personal account and follow the on-screen instructions to complete your application. 

IMPORTANT STUDENT ADVISORY

If you are uncertain about specific documentation requirements, deadlines, or further eligibility criteria not explicitly detailed here, you should verify all information directly through the official HELB website at https://www.helb.co.ke/helb-products/helb-loans/undergraduate-loans/.
